_comment: Reference data for CASE-SPH-WEDGE-ENTRY-2D. Every number carries its provenance. A reference whose original source could not be read is status=WITHHELD with value null; a value reproduced in an open-access peer-reviewed table is kept in a separate 'beta30_via_open_source' field with its coordinates - a recalled or secondary number is never presented as the original table value. Derived analytic values are NOT typed here: run.py computes them from the in-repo implementation into artifacts/case_sph_wedge_entry_2d/refs_derived.json.

case.physical_setup: 2D symmetric rigid wedge, deadrise angle beta = 30 deg (angle between one face and the undisturbed free surface), constant vertical velocity V, calm water, gravity neglected (self-similar regime: the only length scale is V*t)
case.metric: peak slamming pressure coefficient on the wetted wedge surface, Cp_max = p_max / (0.5 rho V^2)

references.role: machine-checkable analytic anchor (primary verdict of this case)
references.citation: Wagner (1932) - classical flat-plate / wedge water-impact solution. Pre-DOI publication: no Crossref record exists, so the anchor is the in-repo derivation and its tests, not an unreadable bibliographic record.
references.formula: C = pi / (2 tan beta); Cp_centre = C; Cp_max = C^2 + 1 (C >= 1)
references.provenance_kind: closed-form analytic solution of the same idealisation (inviscid, incompressible, potential flow, jet ignored, gravity neglected)
references.caveat: small-deadrise asymptotic theory. Per the Z&F (1993) abstract (publisher-deposited, retrieved via OpenAlex) the Wagner asymptotic 'agrees with the similarity solution for small alpha', so at beta = 30 deg a SPH-vs-Wagner error is NOT the same quantity as SPH-vs-Z&F; it is reported as the case's analytic anchor and is not substituted for the withheld Z&F comparison.

references.citation: Zhao, R. & Faltinsen, O. (1993) Water entry of two-dimensional bodies. Journal of Fluid Mechanics 246, 593-612. DOI 10.1017/S002211209300028X

bibliographic_verification.crossref: GET https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1017/s002211209300028x -> HTTP 200, title='Water entry of two-dimensional bodies', volume=246, page=593-612, authors=[Zhao R. (first), Faltinsen O.]

references.abstract_obtained: A numerical method for studying water entry of a two-dimensional body of arbitrary cross-section is presented. It is a nonlinear boundary element method with a jet flow approximation. The method has been verified by comparisons with new similarity solution results for wedges with deadrise angles varying from 4 to 81 degrees. A simple asymptotic solution for small deadrise angles alpha based on Wagner (1932) agrees with the similarity solution for small alpha.
references.abstract_provenance: OpenAlex record W2051783622, abstract_inverted_index (publisher-deposited abstract), retrieved 2026-11-12
references.withheld_reason: The beta = 30 deg number lives in the paper's tables/figures; the article is closed access (OpenAlex oa_status=closed, no repository full text) and the ecosystem has no document-delivery channel and no registered copy (checked 2026-11-12: knowledge_base LIKE '%zhao|faltinsen|wedge|deadrise%' -> 0 numeric rows; oss_solutions -> 0 rows). Reporting a remembered or secondary-source number as the original table value would be fabrication, so the cell stays empty and the comparison is WITHHELD (not PASS, not FAIL).
references.what_would_close_it: The paper delivered to the repo as a text-extractable file (PDF/text) with page/table coordinates for the wedge similarity-solution pressure coefficient at beta = 30 deg; then the digitised value is entered here with page/table/figure coordinates and the comparison re-run with --stage accept (no solver change needed).

beta30_via_open_source.note: The primary article is still unread in the ecosystem, so table_or_figure_value_beta_30 stays null and the primary status stays WITHHELD. This field is a *tracked secondary* value: a peer-reviewed open-access table that states it reproduces the Zhao & Faltinsen composite solution. It is usable as the acceptance denominator only with that provenance attached, and it is cross-checked against the independent exact similarity value (EIM = 3.45, i.e. 0.3 % apart), which is what makes it credible.

references.role: open-access primary source for the peak slamming pressure coefficient at beta = 30 deg, including the Zhao & Faltinsen (1993) composite solution (column COM) and the exact self-similar solution of Dobrovol'skaya (1969) (column EIM) evaluated by Wang & Faltinsen (2017)
references.citation: Jain, U., Novakovic, V., Bogaert, H. & van der Meer, D. (2022) On wedge-slamming pressures. Journal of Fluid Mechanics 934, A26. DOI 10.1017/jfm.2021.1129. Open-access preprint arXiv:2011.10378v3 used for the numbers (ar5iv HTML full text).

bibliographic_verification.crossref: GET https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=On+wedge-slamming+pressures+Jain+van+der+Meer -> HTTP 200, DOI 10.1017/jfm.2021.1129, container JFM vol 934, authors [Jain, Novakovic, Bogaert, van der Meer]
bibliographic_verification.fulltext: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.10378 -> HTTP 200, 373 kB HTML, text-extracted with a tag-stripping script (no pdftotext in the image); all numbers below were parsed out of that text, not recalled.

references.table_coordinates: Table 1 (section 2.4.2), caption: 'Values of C_p,max (== P_max/rho V^2) for several deadrise angles beta'

column_legend.GWM: generalised Wagner model (Korobkin 2004, pressure eq. 21 of the source)
column_legend.EIM: exact self-similar integral equation, Dobrovol'skaya (1969), numerical results of Wang & Faltinsen (2017)
column_legend.COM: composite solution of Zhao & Faltinsen (1993) -- the mission-designated metric owner
column_legend.Sensor1: space-averaged measurement, transducer 1 (not a point pressure: not comparable to a point Cp_max)

references.normalisation: Cp_max in this table is defined as P_max / (rho V^2). The case's own Cp is P / (0.5 rho V^2), so every table value is multiplied by 2 before use (regrade.py: cp_q_units()). Mixing the two normalisations is a factor-2 error, which is exactly the class of defect audited in docs/audit_wagner_pressure_reference_m17079.md.

pressure_profile_equation.used_for: independent re-derivation of the in-repo Wagner profile (see literature_refs.wagner_eq10_over_q)

wetting_rate_equation.statement: c(t) = pi V t / (2 tan beta)

integrity_checks.monotone_in_beta: every model column decreases with beta (test enforces it: catches an OCR/typing error)
integrity_checks.ASM_vs_asymptotic: column ASM must equal the Wagner-family leading order C^2/2 (in rho V^2 units) within 1 % for beta >= 10 deg, C = pi/(2 tan beta) -- ties the digitised table to the in-repo C, so a wrong normalisation cannot pass

references.provenance_kind: peer-reviewed open-access table of solutions; secondary as regards the Zhao & Faltinsen (1993) numbers it reproduces
